samples.summary: The `d<id>` host-div cleanup added in the `finally` block has no test at all
samples.evidence: `renderPass` deliberately removes mermaid's layout host div unconditionally (`document.getElementById(`d${id}`)?.remove()`, mermaid.ts:477-485) with a long comment explaining that otherwise a failing parse leaks one host containing un-DOMPurified engine output per keystroke. No test in preview.test.ts (nor editor.test.ts) ever asserts anything about `document.body` after a render pass; and the stub engine (`stubEngine`, preview.test.ts:243-250) never creates such a host div, so no existing case could fail if the `finally` block were deleted. A stub that appends `d<id>` before resolving/throwing would make it testable. Searched: grep for `getElementById`, `document.body` and `d${id}`/`dnote-mermaid` in packages/notes/src.

samples.summary: The extended `SECURE_KEYS` list (and `startOnLoad: false`) passed to `mermaid.initialize` is never asserted
samples.evidence: SECURE_KEYS (mermaid.ts:167-184) is documented as one of the three security layers — it is what pins `themeCSS`/`themeVariables`/`htmlLabels` against nested directive overrides. The only assertions on the initialize config are `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark' })` (preview.test.ts:744-746) and `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'strict' })` (preview.test.ts:776-778). Removing or truncating `secure: SECURE_KEYS`, or flipping `startOnLoad`, would leave the whole suite green. Since the engine is stubbed, asserting the config object is the only coverage available and it is not taken.

samples.summary: Failure caching — an explicit design decision — has no test
samples.evidence: `remember(key, result)` is called for error results too (mermaid.ts:466-486) and the doc comment on `renderCache` (mermaid.ts:88-98) plus docs/tasks/active/...-lessons.md ('Cache the failures too') present this as the fix for re-parsing on every keystroke. The only failure test ('keeps the source visible and reports the error for invalid syntax', preview.test.ts:316-332) renders once and never re-renders, so a change that cached only successes (i.e. `if ('node' in result) remember(...)`) would not fail any test. The cache-hit tests (preview.test.ts:679-698, 749-762) all use the success path.
searchedFor: preview.test.ts search for a second render of a failing source

samples.summary: The 'bump the pass counter even when nothing is pending' guard is untested
samples.evidence: mermaid.ts:400-406 bumps `passSeq` before `collectPending` specifically so that a re-render with NO mermaid fence still supersedes an in-flight pass. The supersession test (preview.test.ts:610-643) re-renders with a fence, so the generation would be bumped by the normal path anyway; moving the bump after the `pending.length === 0` early return would keep every test green. No case renders fence -> (park pass) -> render fence-free markdown and asserts the stale block stays unpainted.

samples.summary: The mermaid source-fallback contrast fix (the one defect a browser found) has no regression coverage anywhere
samples.evidence: The new `.note-mermaid .note-mermaid-source { color: #24292e }` rule exists precisely because `prose` styled the bare `<pre>` near-white on `#f6f8fa` (1.16:1), documented in docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-lessons.md:103-116 as breaking the 'always degrades to readable source' property the design rests on. The repo has an enforced visual harness (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/*-scenarios.tsx) but there is no notes or mermaid scenario there, and grep for 'mermaid' across the repo finds no test outside packages/notes unit tests, which run in jsdom and assert no styles. Deleting this rule reintroduces the exact shipped defect with a green pipeline.

samples.summary: Every mermaid test stubs the engine, so nothing verifies the sanitizer config against real mermaid output
samples.evidence: All cases construct `NotePreview({ mermaidLoader: async () => stubEngine(...) })` and hand-written SVG fixtures stand in for engine output (explicitly acknowledged at preview.test.ts:229-230 and 517-522: 'Real mermaid cannot run under jsdom, so this fixture stands in for its output'). The risky interaction — whether PURIFY_CONFIG's narrowed `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP`, FORBID_TAGS and `<style>`-drop rules leave a real diagram intact — is therefore asserted only against fixtures the same author wrote, and the project's own lessons file (line 103) records that this stubbing already hid a shipped defect. `stripConfigDirectives` is likewise only checked against the stub's recorded argument, never against what mermaid actually parses.
searchedFor: glob for integration/browser tests importing mermaid

samples.summary: The editor no longer builds an untheme-seeded preview (`new NotePreview({ theme })`), but no editor test asserts the seed
samples.evidence: editor.ts:177 changed to `new NotePreview({ theme })`. The new editor tests (editor.test.ts:188-270) cover the repaint, the `setTheme` push and the hidden-preview skip, but none asserts that a preview created with `initialize(..., 'dark', ...)` starts with the dark mermaid palette — reverting to `new NotePreview()` would keep them all green (the preview-side seed test at preview.test.ts:735-747 constructs NotePreview directly, bypassing the editor).

preview.ts adds `if (lang.toLowerCase() === 'mermaid')`. Every test fence in preview.test.ts uses lowercase ```mermaid; no case asserts that ```Mermaid or ```MERMAID (or `mermaid` with a trailing info word) takes the diagram path rather than the highlighted-code path.

samples.summary: apply() clearing a stale error message on a later success is untested
samples.evidence: `apply()` removes any existing `.note-mermaid-message` and the ERROR_ATTR before painting a successful render (mermaid.ts:491-500). No test walks a block from the error state to the success state, so dropping the `querySelector(MESSAGE_CLASS)?.remove()` line would leave a 'Diagram error' label above a correctly rendered diagram with the suite still green.

finding.summary: The `d<id>` host-div cleanup added in the `finally` block has no test at all
finding.evidence: `renderPass` deliberately removes mermaid's layout host div unconditionally (`document.getElementById(`d${id}`)?.remove()`, mermaid.ts:477-485) with a long comment explaining that otherwise a failing parse leaks one host containing un-DOMPurified engine output per keystroke. No test in preview.test.ts (nor editor.test.ts) ever asserts anything about `document.body` after a render pass; and the stub engine (`stubEngine`, preview.test.ts:243-250) never creates such a host div, so no existing case could fail if the `finally` block were deleted. A stub that appends `d<id>` before resolving/throwing would make it testable. Searched: grep for `getElementById`, `document.body` and `d${id}`/`dnote-mermaid` in packages/notes/src.

verdict.reason: The unconditional `d<id>` host-div cleanup in mermaid.ts's `finally` block (mermaid.ts:477-485) has no test anywhere in the repo. packages/notes has exactly 6 test files; only preview.test.ts and editor.test.ts touch mermaid, and neither asserts anything about document-level leftovers (no `document.body` content/child-count assertions in packages/notes at all). Every engine stub derives from `stubEngine` (preview.test.ts:243-250), whose render implementations either resolve an `{svg}` object or throw (317-319, 387-389, 400-407, 653-660) — none appends a `d<id>` element to document.body, so no existing case could fail if the `finally` block were deleted. Repo-wide greps for `note-mermaid`/`renderMermaidBlocks` and for `mermaid` in non-TS/e2e/script/config files turned up no other coverage (only src, CSS, docs, and prior review artifacts). This is a real, security-motivated behavior (preventing per-keystroke leakage of un-DOMPurified engine output) with zero meaningful coverage: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: The unterminated-directive strip test's only assertion holds even if the strip destroys the whole diagram
finding.evidence: `it('strips an unterminated config directive, which mermaid still reads')` (preview.test.ts:534-546) renders `%%{init: {"themeCSS": ...}` followed by `flowchart LR\n  A-->B` and asserts only `expect(source).not.toContain('themeCSS')`. `DIRECTIVE_RE` (mermaid.ts:209) has the closing `}%%` optional and its fourth alternative `((?:(?!}%{2}).|\r?\n)*)` matches greedily across newlines, so for this input the strip consumes the rest of the fence body and `mermaid.render` is called with (effectively) an empty diagram. The assertion passes regardless. Note the three sibling strip tests (lines 559, 574, 587) DO assert the diagram body survives (`toContain('flowchart LR')` / `startsWith('flowchart LR')`); this one omits exactly that assertion, so it provides no evidence that the documented 'stripped exactly as far as mermaid would have read it' behavior is right — it would pass under a strip that eats everything.

verdict.reason: The test exists as described (at preview.test.ts:554-566, ~20 lines off from the cited range) and its sole assertion is expect(source).not.toContain('themeCSS') — a negative-only check that holds even if the strip consumes the entire fence body. The captured `source` is the stripped text (mermaid.ts:468 passes stripConfigDirectives(source) into mermaid.render), and DIRECTIVE_RE (mermaid.ts:209-210) makes the closing }%% optional with a greedy newline-crossing fourth alternative, so for this input (which contains no }%%) the match extends through the flowchart body, leaving an effectively empty diagram — and the assertion still passes. The three sibling strip tests (lines 579, 594, 607) each assert the body survives; this one omits exactly that, so it gives no evidence for the documented "stripped exactly as far as mermaid would have read it" contract (mermaid.ts:204-207). No other test covers stripConfigDirectives directly (grep found only the definition at mermaid.ts:226, the call site at mermaid.ts:468, and a comment at preview.test.ts:269). Real, in-lane (insufficient/half-vacuous assertion presented as coverage of a behavior claim), major impact.
